candidates.exact_span: The following Minimum Quantification Levels (MQL's) are to be used for reporting pollutant data for NPDES permit applications and/or compliance reporting.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines the table as reporting quantification levels rather than enforceable discharge limits (A); scopes when MQL-based reporting rules attach to permit applications versus compliance reporting, which can bear on whether monitoring/reporting obligations are in play (B); and sets the benchmark for whether a result is ordinarily numeric versus below quantification or otherwise non-comparable (C).

candidates.locator: page 1, section part_i, table column headers
candidates.computation_change_reason: Specifies the units for all tabulated MQL values; a different unit interpretation or conversion relative to permit limits or reported measurements would change numeric limit applicability comparisons (A) and classification of reported or missing values relative to quantification (C).

candidates.locator: page 1, section part_i, METALS table, Mercury row
candidates.computation_change_reason: Lists two different MQL values for Mercury with a footnote marker (*1) whose explanatory text is not present in this segment; differing interpretations of which value applies would change mercury reporting treatment and whether an available measurement can be numerically compared or must be treated as below quantification or unresolved.

candidates.locator: page 1, section part_i, METALS table, Cyanide rows
candidates.computation_change_reason: Distinguishes total cyanide from weak-acid-dissociable cyanide as separate reporting parameters; misidentifying which parameter was monitored or reported would change the applicable limit pairing and missing-evidence or non-detect handling even though both MQL values are numerically identical.

candidates.locator: page 1, section part_i, METALS table, Thallium row
candidates.computation_change_reason: The pollutant name is misspelled ('Thalllium'); uncertainty over whether this row governs thallium reporting for a given measurement would change parameter matching across limit applicability (A), monitoring/reporting requirement identification (B), and missing-evidence classification (C).

candidates.locator: page 1, section part_i, VOLATILE COMPOUNDS table, Chlorodibromomethane row
candidates.computation_change_reason: The pollutant name is misspelled ('Clorodibromomethane'); uncertainty over parameter identity would change which MQL governs reporting and therefore limit pairing, monitoring obligation matching, and missing-evidence treatment for that analyte.
